title: Stephen's Speech and Martyrdom

questions.question: Stephen began his defense by recounting God's call to Abraham. Where was Abraham when God appeared to him before he lived in Haran?
options: In Mesopotamia
In Canaan
In Egypt
In Ur of the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Acts 7:2 (ESV): "Brothers and fathers, hear me. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,"

questions.question: Stephen pointed out that although God promised Canaan to Abraham and his offspring, Abraham never received it himself. What did God say his children would experience first?
options: They would be sojourners in a land not their own and enslaved and mistreated for 400 years
They would wander the desert for forty years without rest
They would be scattered among all the nations of the earth
They would suffer under foreign kings for seven generations
questions.correctAnswer: They would be sojourners in a land not their own and enslaved and mistreated for 400 years
questions.explanation: Acts 7:6 (ESV): "And God spoke to this effect—that his offspring would be sojourners in a land belonging to others, who would enslave them and afflict them four hundred years."

questions.question: Stephen recounted that Joseph was sold into slavery by his brothers. What happened to Joseph in Egypt?
options: God was with him and rescued him from all his afflictions, giving him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh
He was imprisoned for twenty years before Pharaoh released him
He became a slave in Pharaoh's household and worked faithfully
He escaped and returned briefly to Canaan before going back
questions.correctAnswer: God was with him and rescued him from all his afflictions, giving him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Acts 7:9-10 (ESV): "...but God was with him and rescued him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh..."

questions.question: Stephen described Moses' early life. Who did Moses kill, triggering his flight to Midian?
options: An Egyptian who was wronging an Israelite
A guard who beat a slave near the Nile
Pharaoh's overseer in the brick workhouse
A Hebrew who was beating his fellow Hebrew
questions.correctAnswer: An Egyptian who was wronging an Israelite
questions.explanation: Acts 7:24 (ESV): "And seeing one of them being wronged, he defended the oppressed man and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian."

questions.question: God appeared to Moses at the burning bush and called the ground there "holy ground." Where was this?
options: At Mount Sinai in the wilderness
Near the Red Sea entrance
On the border of Egypt and Midian
In the desert of Paran
questions.correctAnswer: At Mount Sinai in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Acts 7:30,33 (ESV): "Now when forty years had passed, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai... Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off the sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.'"

questions.question: Stephen quoted God's promise about a prophet like Moses: "God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your brothers." Who said this originally?
options: Moses himself
Isaiah the prophet
Samuel the prophet
David in the Psalms
questions.explanation: Acts 7:37 (ESV): "This is the Moses who said to the Israelites, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your brothers.'"

questions.question: Stephen accused Israel of rejecting Moses just as they later rejected Jesus. What did the Israelites say to Moses when he tried to reconcile two fighting Hebrews in Egypt?
options: "Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?"
"Go back to Pharaoh's household where you belong."
"We do not recognize you as our leader or deliver."
"You are not one of us; you were raised by Egyptians."
questions.correctAnswer: "Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?"
questions.explanation: Acts 7:27 (ESV): "But the man who was wronging his neighbor thrust him aside, saying, 'Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?'"

questions.question: The Israelites in the wilderness refused to obey Moses and turned to idolatry. What did they make and offer sacrifices to?
options: A golden calf
The image of Baal
A bronze serpent
An Asherah pole
questions.explanation: Acts 7:41 (ESV): "And they made a calf in those days, and offered a sacrifice to the idol and were rejoicing in the works of their hands."

questions.question: Stephen quoted Amos regarding Israel's wilderness idolatry: They carried the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan. God said He would send them into exile beyond what location?
options: Babylon
Egypt
Assyria
Persia
questions.explanation: Acts 7:43 (ESV): "...and I will send you into exile beyond Babylon."

questions.question: Stephen argued that God does not dwell in houses made by hands. He quoted Isaiah: "Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what is the place of my rest?"
options: This was from the prophet Isaiah
This was from the psalms of David
This was from Jeremiah's lamentations
This was from Solomon's dedication prayer
questions.correctAnswer: This was from the prophet Isaiah
questions.explanation: Acts 7:48-49 (ESV) quotes Isaiah 66:1-2: "Yet the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands, as the prophet says, 'Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool....'"

questions.question: Stephen called the council "stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears." He then accused them of always doing what to the Holy Spirit?
options: Resisting the Holy Spirit
Quenching the Holy Spirit
Blaspheming the Holy Spirit
Grieving the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 7:51 (ESV): "You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you."

questions.question: As Stephen was being stoned, he saw a vision. What exactly did he see?
options: The heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God
Jesus descending from heaven with a crown of glory
A throne of fire and God seated upon it in splendor
Angels ascending and descending as at Jacob's ladder
questions.correctAnswer: The heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God
questions.explanation: Acts 7:56 (ESV): "And he said, 'Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.'"

questions.question: As Stephen was dying from the stones, he made two final prayers. What were they?
options: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" and "Lord, do not hold this sin against them"
"Father, forgive them" and "Remember me when you come in your kingdom"
"Lord receive me" and "Let my blood atone for their wickedness"
"Jesus, save me" and "May God judge these men righteously"
questions.correctAnswer: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" and "Lord, do not hold this sin against them"
questions.explanation: Acts 7:59-60 (ESV): "And as they were stoning Stephen, he called out, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.' And falling to his knees he cried out with a loud voice, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them.'"

questions.question: Who was standing there consenting to Stephen's death and watching over the cloaks of those who stoned him?
options: Saul
Caiaphas
Annas
Gamaliel
questions.explanation: Acts 7:58 (ESV): "Then they cast him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul."

questions.question: Which of the following did Stephen NOT accuse the council of in his concluding speech?
options: Worshipping false gods in the temple of Solomon
Betraying and murdering the Righteous One
Receiving the law as delivered by angels but not keeping it
Persecuting the prophets who announced the coming of the Righteous One
questions.correctAnswer: Worshipping false gods in the temple of Solomon
questions.explanation: Acts 7:52-53 (ESV) lists the accusations: persecuting prophets, betraying and murdering the Righteous One, and not keeping the Law. Temple worship of false gods is not among these final charges.

key_verse_text: "Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
